correctness.rationale: The domain is exactly 1/4<|z|<1 with Euclidean boundary arclength and positive smooth nonradial phi=|z-2/3|^2. Multiplication by z-p is an isometry onto unweighted H^2 functions vanishing at p, and the rank-one compressed reproducing kernel has numerator D(w)=H(w)H(p²)-H(p)H(pw). The two selected negative test values and p²,p,pw fall in Laurent convergence annulus; exact Fraction evaluations give D32(-3/8)>19/100 and D32(-3/4)<-9/100. Explicit bilateral tails imply |D-D32|<24E32<1/125, so the intermediate value theorem gives genuine boundary-to-interior zero. The result asserts existence only, not uniqueness.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Standard annulus Laurent series and rank-one reproducing-kernel projection are general methods but neither yields the signs of the specific determinant. Jain–Verma explicitly leave boundary-to-interior zeros open under smooth positive weights; their nonvanishing holomorphic-factor identity cannot apply because this factor vanishes at p.

originality.rationale: The explicit nonradial positive weight yielding a boundary-to-interior weighted Szegő kernel zero directly supplies an example requested in Jain–Verma Remark 5.7(1). Their Example 5.3 assumes a holomorphic factor nonvanishing on the closed domain, whereas q=z-2/3 has an interior zero and forces a rank-one compression. The related published rotation-invariant annular family and derivative-zero theorems do not cover the same assertion. Best-of-knowledge PASS.
